title: Logarithms
examples: When should I use the change of base formula?
What is the difference between log base 10 and ln?
Can I solve for x if it is in the exponent?

explain.say: Today we will learn about logarithms. A logarithm is simply the inverse of an exponential function. It asks what power you must raise a number to get another number. For example, we can write log base 10 of 100. This asks what power of 10 gives you 100. The answer is two because 10 squared equals 100.

draw.text: logb(x) = y ext{ means } b^y = x

explain.say: We have several important laws for logarithms. The logarithm of a product is the sum of the logarithms. So, log of A times B equals the log of A plus the log of B. For instance, log of 100 times 1000 equals the log of 100 plus the log of 1000.

The logarithm of a quotient is the difference of the logarithms. This is very useful for simplifying expressions. For example, log of 100 divided by 10 equals the log of 100 minus the log of 10. The result is two minus one, which is one.

Sometimes we need to change the base of a logarithm. The change of base formula is very helpful here. It states that log base B of A equals the natural logarithm of A divided by the natural logarithm of B. So, log base 2 of 8 equals the natural log of 8 divided by the natural log of 2.

Finally, we look at solving exponential equations using logarithms. If we have an equation like 3 to the power of x equals 20. We take the natural logarithm of both sides. This gives us x equals the natural log of 20 divided by the natural log of 3. This method lets us solve for x when it is in the exponent.

draw.text: If b^x = y, then x = ln(y) / ln(b)

faq.q: What is the natural logarithm, ln?
faq.a: The natural logarithm uses the mathematical constant e as its base. It is the logarithm to the base e. You might also see it written as log base e.
asks: What is the base for ln?

faq.q: When can I use the change of base formula?
faq.a: You use this formula when you need to calculate a logarithm but your calculator only has base 10 or base e. It lets you change any base to one of those two.
asks: How do I change the base?
What if my calculator does not have base 5?

faq.q: Is log base 10 the same as common logarithm?
faq.a: Yes, log base 10 is often called the common logarithm. It is used frequently in science and engineering calculations. It is the logarithm to the base 10.
asks: Is log base 10 the same thing?

faq.q: Does the product rule work for logarithms?
faq.a: Yes, the product rule states that the log of a product is the sum of the logs. This means log of A times B equals log of A plus log of B. This helps simplify multiplication problems.
asks: How do I handle multiplication with logs?
Can I add logs if they are multiplied?

faq.q: If I have 5 to the power of x equals 125, do I need logs?
faq.a: No, you can solve that by rewriting 125 as 5 cubed. So, 5 to the power of x equals 5 to the power of three. This means x must equal three.
asks: Can I solve this without logarithms?
What if the number was not a clean power of 5?

facts: The logarithm base b of b equals one. This is because b to the power of one is b.
The logarithm base b of one always equals zero. This is because b to the power of zero is one.
The natural logarithm, ln, uses the mathematical constant e as its base.
Logarithms and exponentials are inverse operations of each other.
